messages:
maya: Quick scorecard for meridian-9b bring-up. TL;DR: int8 looks like the safest default for chat — int4 cuts ~28% unit cost but we see a consistent quality hit on multi-turn/recall slices (~8–12%). Recs at bottom.
ev: Can you paste the core numbers and which slices failed?
maya: Sure — pasted raw snapshot below (small sample, averaged):
```
p50    : 70ms (int8) / 65ms (int4)
p95    : 420ms (int8) / 380ms (int4)
99.9   : 1.2s (int8) / 1.7s (int4)  # kv-cache tail weirdness under concurrency
avg tokens/req: 120
cost/1k tokens: $0.007 (int8) / $0.005 (int4)
quality delta (multi-turn recall set): int4 = -9% F1, -11% ROUGE-L
quality delta (single-turn instr): int4 = -2% accuracy
```
zoe: Noted the 99.9 spike — I saw similar in manual QA: hallucination rate up on conversational QA slice for int4.
lee: Backend note — int4 memory usage is lower but we hit a kernel path that increases tail latency when KV cache churns. Might be mitigated with a short-lived cache warmup strategy.
sam: From product POV: GTN cares about perceived quality for core chat flows. We should avoid defaulting free/premium users to int4 for chat. But embeddings/batch summarization is a good int4 candidate.
product-rachel: Agreed. Proposal: default routing -> meridian-9b-int8 for chat; meridian-9b-int4 for background/batch; premium users pinned to int8. Can we canary? 10% traffic for 72h and watch quality signals.
maya: Proposed hybrid routing snippet for ops (minimal):
```
routing:
  default: meridian-9b-int8
  fallback: meridian-9b-int4
  rules:
    - if prompt_tokens > 512 -> meridian-9b-int8
    - if workload in ["summarization","batch-embed"] -> meridian-9b-int4
    - if user_tier == "premium" -> meridian-9b-int8
    - monitor: slice("multi-turn-recall") -> alert if quality_drop > 5%
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary rollout (10%) -> meridian-9b-int8 on prod-us-west-1. Link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/rollout/6723456789
maya: Timeline: 72h canary. Need: p95/p99, cost delta, slice-level quality for: multi-turn-recall, conversational-QA, longform-coherence, instruction-following.
ev: I'll wire the eval harness and realtime signal watchers. Will add dashboards and a regression alert (quality delta > 5% on any primary slice).
zoe: I'll run a 200-sample qualitative pass on the int4 holdback pool for the same slices and flag hallucination examples.
lee: Ops followups: capture KV-cache hit rates, CPU/SM utilization, and tail latencies. If 99.9 exceeds 2s we rollback int4 path.
maya: Decision for now: canary int8 default (10%); keep int4 in a small holdback pool for batch/embs; do NOT route free chat traffic to int4. Re-evaluate after 72h with collected signals.
sam: Action items:
 - evan: set up eval dashboards + regression alerts (ETA 6h)
 - zoe: qualitative pass on int4 holdback (ETA 24h)
 - lee: telemetry patch for KV-cache + tail alerts (ETA 12h)
 - maya: draft GTN recommendation doc based on canary results (ETA after 72h)
product-rachel: Thanks — sounds like a pragmatic plan. Keep product looped on any >3% regression.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started at 6723456792. Canary traffic partition: 10%.
maya: 👍 I'll post a short update after first 12h sample.
